At the start of a run, all 5 characters have access to a starting deck of 10 or 12 cards. Each character has their own version of Strike and Defend, all of which function identically, save their appearance. In addition to these Strikes and Defends, each character has 1-2 starting cards that help enable and distinguish their starting deck's composition.

{{TOC_limit|3}}

== Card Types ==
All cards in the game can be sorted into one of these five types.

* {{C2|Pommel Strike| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}} are cards that deal direct damage and sometimes have a secondary effect. These cards have a rectangular border with the bottom edge being tapered down to a trapezoid.
* {{C2|Blur| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Skill|Skills}} are cards that have diverse effects usually through providing {{KW2|Block}}, utilities, buffs, or debuffs. They are distinct from Attack cards due to never dealing damage directly, however they are capable of doing so indirectly via debuffs (such as {{BD2|Poison}}) or utilities (such as {{2|Defect}}'s orbs). These cards have a rectangular border.
* {{C2|Tyranny| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} are cards that give a buff that lasts throughout the combat encounter. Each copy of a power can only be played once per combat. Some powers give flat stat bonuses (such as {{BD2|Strength}} or {{BD2|Dexterity}}), require certain conditions to be met during combat, or even provide unique buffs that can drastically alter playstyle. These cards have a rectangular border with the bottom edge being tapered down to an oval.
* {{C2|Burn| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Status|Statuses}} are cards added to your deck temporarily by the various monsters of the Spire or as a cost to playing specific cards from the Defect or the Regent. Most often, Statuses are added to hinder you in some way: either by taking the place of beneficial draws, or by causing damage to you if left in your hand at the end of turn. Status cards that damage you at the end of the are automaticlaly discarded even if you have {{R2|Runic Pyramid}} or if you give them {{KW2|Retain}}. Statuses are removed from the deck at the end of combat.
* {{C2|Bad Luck| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}} are {{KW2|Unplayable}} or otherwise detrimental cards added to the deck during in-game events. They are similar to Status cards but they persist in the deck until removed by other means and typically have more severe effects, such as direct HP loss, losing {{2|Gold}}, or applying {{BD2|Weak}}/{{BD2|Frail}}. Like Statuses, Curses that affect you at the end of turn, such as {{C2|Bad Luck}}, will be discarded even if you have {{R2|Runic Pyramid}} or if you give them {{KW2|Retain}}. {{C2|Enthralled}} and {{C2|Spore Mind}} are the only Curses that can be played. Some Curses cannot be removed from your deck at all; these Curses have the {{KW2|Eternal}} tag.
* {{C2|Byrdonis Egg| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Quest|Quests}} are {{KW2|Unplayable}} cards added to the deck during in-game events that have postponed, powerful rewards. There are four quest cards in the game: {{C2|Byrdonis Egg}}, {{C2|Dowsing}}, {{C2|Lantern Key}}, and {{C2|Spoils Map}}. When you complete the quest, the associated quest card is removed; until then, it serves effectively as an {{KW2|Unplayable}} curse.
** Curses and Quest cards cannot be {{KW2|Enchant|Enchanted}}.

=== Multiplayer ===
There are 37 {{2|Multiplayer#Multiplayer_Cards|Multiplayer exclusive cards}}, 5 for each character and 12 Colorless.

== Card Rarity ==
The rarity of the card is indicated in the color of the banner behind the name.

* {{C2|Bodyguard| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Basic|Basic}} cards are the default cards from the starting deck for your character. They have the same ''grey'' banner and border as Commons, though you cannot find them in card rewards or transform cards into them.
* {{C2|Pommel Strike| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Common|Common}} cards have a ''grey'' banner. There are no Common Colorless cards.
* {{C2|Blur| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} cards have a {{TS|blue||''blue''}} banner and border.
* {{C2|Tyranny| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} cards have a {{TS|gold||''golden''}} banner and border.
* {{C2|Apotheosis| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Ancient|Ancient}} cards have a ''faint-prismatic'' banner (''white'' on the mini-tooltip), a blue flame at the top, and feature an invisible border as their cards are full-art (but there is still a shape for the banner on the card to differentiate between Attacks, Skills, and Powers). They can only be obtained from {{2|Ancients}}, with most Ancients offering one way to add an Ancient card and/or transform a Basic card into an Ancient card.
* {{C2|Stack| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Event|Event}} cards are only obtained from {{2|Events}}. Event cards from the Act 1 event {{E2|Trash Heap}} appear to be character-specific, however they are actually still considered Colorless and can be obtained by any character. They have a {{TS|green||''green''}} banner and border.
* {{C2|Shiv| }} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Token|Token}} cards are cards that are generated in combat by various cards that the player plays. They are similar to Status Cards, but they all have a tangible benefit as opposed to a downside, such as {{C2|Shiv}} and {{C2|Soul}}. Like Statuses, Token cards cannot be added to your permanent deck. Even though Tokens are often associated with a particular character, they are all classified and displayed as Colorless.
** This is the Slay the Spire 2 equivalent of {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Special|Special}} cards from Slay the Spire 1.

=== Card Distribution ===
The chance to get a Rare card in a card reward starts off at an offset of minus 5%. The offset is then added to the base chance (see tables below) for a rare for the final rare chance. For each card rolled that is ''not'' a Rare card, this offset is incremented by 1% ({{Asc2|7|0.5%}}), up to maximum of 40%. Card rewards that are skipped will still affect this counter.

When a Rare card is rolled, the offset resets back to the initial value, minus 5%. As a result, your first card reward in Act 1, Act 2 and Act 3 can never have a Rare card (barring {{2|Ancient}} relics such as {{R2|Arcane Scroll}}). The change to the offset happens immediately after generating a card, which means it is adjusted 3 times in a regular card reward. For example, if the first 2 cards generated were non-rare, the third card now has a 2% ({{Asc2|7|1%}}) higher chance to be a rare. 

{{Asc2|7|Ascension}} halves the base chance to get a rare, as well as the increment when not seeing a rare card. 

Card rewards from {{2|Bosses}} always generate only Rare cards.

The full calculation is then as follows:
* Get the current '''offset''' (default -5%).
* Get the '''base rare chance''' based on the room you're in (see tables below).
* Add those two together to get the '''current rare chance'''.
* Roll a number between 0 and 1, if it is less than the '''current rare chance''' the card is rare. The '''offset''' is then reset to -5%. Continue with the next card.
* If the number is greater than the '''current rare chance''', compare it to the '''base uncommon chance''' (see below) plus the '''current rare chance'''. If the number is less then that, the card is uncommon. Increase the '''offset''' by 1% ({{Asc2|7|0.5%}}) and continue with the next card.
* If none of the above apply, then the card is common. Increase the '''offset''' by 1% ({{Asc2|7|0.5%}}) and continue with the next card.

Note: Adding the '''current rare chance''' to the '''base uncommon chance''' has the following implications:
* If the '''current rare chance''' is 0 or greater, the uncommon chance is fixed at the values below. The chance for a common card the fills up the rest of the percentages.
* If the '''current rare chance''' is negative, the uncommon chance is decreased by that same amount. For the first card generated in a run after the first hallway fight the odds are then as follows: 
** Rare: -5% + 3% = -2% (can't be generated)
** Uncommon: 37% - 2% = 35%
** Common: 100% - 0% - 35% = 65%

Only cards from card rewards (including {{R2|Orrery}}) affect the offset. Shop Cards do not change the rare offset, however they are affected by it. {{R2|Orrery}} works like 5 sequential card rewards, except it uses the base chance of Shops. That is, it both affects and is affected by the offset.

Effects that generate cards mid-combat as well as some {{2|Events}} are unaffected by Card Rarity and will pick a card uniformly across all available options or from a specific rarity based on the event.

Note: The above percentages are taken directly from the game code and might not add up to 100% exactly due to [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floating-point_arithmetic#Accuracy_problems floating point errors].

== Upgraded Cards ==
Card rewards can include {{KW2|Upgrade|Upgraded}} cards. By default, each non-rare card being offered in a card reward has the following chances of being upgraded:
{| class="wikitable"
!Act
|Percentage
|-
!Act 1
|0%
|-
!Act 2
|25% ({{Asc2|7|12.5%}})
|-
!Act 3
|50% ({{Asc2|7|25%}})
|}

See {{2|Upgrade#Sources_of_Upgraded_Cards|Sources of Upgraded Cards}} for {{2|Relics}} that upgrade some or all cards in a card reward.

== Card Generation ==
Cards can be ''temporarily'' added to a deck via Cards (such as {{C2|Infernal Blade}}, {{C2|White Noise}}, or {{C2|Dirge}}), {{2|Potions}} (such as {{P2|Power Potion}} or {{P2|Colorless Potion}}), {{2|Relics}} (Such as {{R2|Choices Paradox}} or {{R2|Toolbox}}), {{KW2|Transform|Transformations}} (Such as {{C2|Entropy}}), or [[Slay the Spire 2:Monsters|enemy]] attacks (such as {{C2|Frantic Escape}} or {{C2|Slimed}}).
* Certain cards, relics, and enemy attacks will generate specific {{QueryLink2|Cards|rarity:Token|Token}} cards or {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Status|Statuses}} for the duration of the fight.
* Randomly generated cards are equally likely to be {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Common|Common}}, {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Uncommon|Uncommon}}, or {{QueryLink2|Cards|type:Rare|Rare}}, with other Card Rarities being unable to be generated by random effects. Generated cards can only be from the current character, regardless of {{R2|Prismatic Gem}} or {{2|Custom Mode}} modifiers.
* Cards never generate {{KW2|Upgrade|Upgraded}} or {{KW|Enchant|enchanted|2}} unless the card generating specifies that it comes upgraded (such as {{C2|Manifest Authority|Manifest Authority+}}) or enchanted (such as {{C2|Shiv|Shivs}} generated by {{C2|Blade of Ink}}).
* Certain cards are exempt from generating, notably cards that have/enable permanent scaling and/or cards that generate out-of-battle resources. These cards are:
** {{C2|Feed}}
** {{C2|Not Yet}}
** {{C2|Nightmare}}
** {{C2|The Hunt}}
** {{C2|Royalties}}
** {{C2|Eidolon}}
** {{C2|Transfigure}}
** {{C2|Alchemize}}
** {{C2|Hand of Greed}}
** {{C2|Hidden Gem}}

== Sources of Other Characters' Cards ==
Some cards, relics, and events allow you to obtain cards from a character other than the one you are currently playing. Below is a list of ways to obtain them.
* {{C2|Splash}} - Choose 1 of 3 random Attacks from another character to add into your Hand. It's free to play this turn.
* {{R2|Kaleidoscope}} - Upon pickup, obtain 2 card rewards from other characters.
* {{R2|Prismatic Gem}} - Card rewards now contain cards from other colors.
* {{R2|Sea Glass}} - See 15 cards from another character. Choose any number of them to add to your Deck.
* {{E2|Colorful Philosophers}} - Gives 3 card rewards from a selected character.
* Some [[sts2:Custom Mode|Custom Mode]] modifiers:
** {{KW2|Ironclad Cards}} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|color:Ironclad|Ironclad cards}} will now appear in rewards and shops.
** {{KW2|Silent Cards}} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|color:Silent|Silent cards}} will now appear in rewards and shops.
** {{KW2|Regent Cards}} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|color:Regent|Regent cards}} will now appear in rewards and shops.
** {{KW2|Necrobinder Cards}} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|color:Necrobinder|Necrobinder cards}} will now appear in rewards and shops.
** {{KW2|Defect Cards}} - {{QueryLink2|Cards|color:Defect|Defect cards}} will now appear in rewards and shops.

== Beta Art ==
Beta Art is a feature that allows you to replace the normal card art with the early development version of the card art. These often include various puns or references to other popular media.

Beta Art for a character's cards is unlocked when beating the {{M|Corrupt Heart}}. Beta art for {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards and {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curses}} are unlocked after beating the {{M|Corrupt Heart}} with all characters.

Beta art is toggled for each card individually.
* '''For PC:''' Right click to inspect a card at any point and then toggle on the '''Beta Art''' option. Inspecting a card through the Compendium also shows this toggle.
* '''For Console/Mobile:''' Inspect a card in the Compendium and toggle on '''Beta Art'''.
!-->

== Notes ==
* Cards shown as X-cost can still be played even without any {{KW2|Energy}}, although this makes their effects do nothing unless X is increased by some amount. For example, an {{KW2|Upgrade|Upgraded}} {{C2|Multi-Cast}} will {{KW2|Evoke}} one {{2|Orbs|Orb}} even if played without any {{KW2|Energy}}. This can be used to advance the effects of relics such as {{R2|Letter Opener}} and {{R2|Nunchaku}} without spending any {{KW2|Energy}}.
* Any {{KW2|Energy}} icons found on {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless Cards}} will be replaced with the current character's {{KW2|Energy}} icons in game.
